subject: Dedicated reservation options & phased onramp — LakePoint proposal
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakepoint.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood Dedicated options — sizing and timeline

Evelyn — thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the internal perf tests and want to scope a Dedicated reservation to support our inference needs for two models: a 7B chat model for product UX and a 13B reranker. Key constraints: steady state 1k qps of lightweight chat (avg 64 tokens), peak batch reranks (up to 250 concurrent requests, 512 tokens).

Our priorities are predictable latency (p95 < 250ms for chat), cost visibility, and a clear ramp to production over 12 weeks. Can you outline reservation options (cluster size, min GPUs, warm pool, ramp schedule) and call out recommended burst lanes or fallback variants? Also include a ballpark monthly commit cost so finance can triage.

Thanks — Daniel
LakePoint AI
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakepoint.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated options — sizing and timeline

Daniel — appreciate the performance numbers. Attached is a first-pass offer and an accompanying ramp/cost workbook. High-level options below (summary; see attachment for full model-specific assumptions):

Option A — Compact baseline (cost-efficient)
- Cluster: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared across kernels)
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 12 (floor to protect throughput)
- Warm pool: 2 GPUs prewarmed for canary/health checks
- Ramp schedule: Week 0: 25% active (4 GPUs), Week 4: 50% (8 GPUs), Week 8: 75% (12 GPUs), Week 12: 100% (16 GPUs)
- Burst: On-demand burst up to +8 GPUs for <6 hours/day via preconfigured burst lanes
- Expected p95 chat latency: ~180-220ms at steady state (assumes FP16 quantized chat path)

Option B — Production anchor (recommended for predictable UX)
- Cluster: 48x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 36
- Warm pool: 6 GPUs (rolling warmup for zero-cold-start)
- Ramp: Week 0: 20% active, Week 6: 60%, Week 12: 100% (full activation) with automated scaling windows for peak rerank windows
- Burst: +16 GPUs reserved for scheduled peaks (billing anchored to usage)
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime; contract-level latency SLOs can be added to the SOW

Option C — Aggressive throughput (for heavy rerankers)
- Cluster: 96 GPUs with mixed GPU types (higher memory + cheaper throughput lanes)
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 72
- Warm pool: 10 GPUs; accelerated KV-cache sizing for reranker
- Ramp: compressed 8-week onramp to reach 70% then add remaining 30% after production validation

Notes & tradeoffs:
- Min guaranteed GPUs protect tail latency and cold-starts but increase committed cost — we can convert unused commit to credits used for burst if you prefer flexibility.
- Prewarm credits: first-month onboarding includes 5k prewarm credits (covers ramp spikes and smoke tests).
- Model variants: we recommend quantized variants for chat and mixed precision for reranker to balance memory and throughput.

Next steps: tell me which option(s) you want formalized and I’ll share a redline-ready offer + SOW.

— Evelyn
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakepoint.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated options — sizing and timeline

Looping in a quick ops note — given LakePoint's peak rerank batch sizes, we should call out the following in the proposal: 

- Network egress tuning: ensure RDMA topology for intra-cluster allreduce to keep multi-GPU batching latency sub-50ms.
- KV cache sizing: recommend reserving ~120GB of KV capacity per 16 GPUs for the chat model to avoid spill to CPU.
- Activation windows: propose two scheduled peak windows (US morning and US evening) where pre-scheduled burst lanes are primed; these windows can be separate billing buckets.

Also suggest an optional canary: 4-GPU canary cluster in a different AZ for rollback testing (small extra cost but high reliability).
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakepoint.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated options — sizing and timeline

Evelyn / team — minor edits for pricing cadence and commitment terms before we share the formal PDF:

- Monthly commit tiers: offer 3 pricing bands tied to % activation (30%, 60%, 100%) with linear step-down credits for underutilization.
- Early termination: pro-rate credit model after 90 days; requires 30-day notice for decommit trigger.
- Onboarding SLA: include one full runbook handover and two on-call shadowing weeks.

I'll update the workbook (LP_Ramp_Cost_Model.xlsx) with these bands and run sensitivity at 60% utilization. Evelyn — if you agree, we should add a short paragraph in the attachment clarifying the credit conversion for unused commit.

-Rishi
VP, Product Partnerships
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakepoint.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated options — sizing and timeline

Evelyn / Rishi / Karthik — this looks very helpful. LakePoint prefers Option B (Production anchor) with the two scheduled peak windows and the canary AZ. A few asks before we sign: 

1) Finalize monthly pricing bands and include a sample invoice for month 1 and month 4 (post-ramp).
2) Add a 4-week training transfer and two-week shadowing into the SOW (we need ops to be self-sufficient).
3) Confirm burst lane activation latency (time to spin up + docker/pull warm) — we’d like <7 minutes for scheduled bursts.

If you can get the redline-ready offer and SOW by EOD next Wednesday (2026-12-02), we’ll route to procurement. Attachments to reference in the contract: LakePoint_Dedicated_Offer_v1.pdf and the cost workbook.

Thanks — Daniel
